question: A 10 kg child is ordered 50 mg per kg per day of a syrup in four divided doses. The nurse gives each dose as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 125 mg

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Fifty multiplied by ten gives 500 mg for the day, and divided by four this is 125 mg for each dose

🔍 Key Clues: 10 kg

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 250 mg: 250 mg is half the day's dose in one take

C — 100 mg: 100 mg would be only four fifths of a dose

D — 150 mg: 150 mg is more than the order

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The weight is written on the chart and the dose worked out afresh each time, because a child's dose is never taken as a fraction of an adult dose by guesswork

question: The sublingual route avoids the first pass effect because the drug is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. absorbed into the veins under the tongue and carried to the heart before the liver

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The veins under the tongue drain into the general circulation, so the drug reaches the heart before it can pass through the liver

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rubbed into the skin: Rubbing into the skin is the topical route

B — swallowed with water: A swallowed drug passes through the liver first

C — pushed into an arm muscle: An injection into the muscle enters the muscle and not the space under the tongue

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps a sublingual tablet under the tongue and does not let the patient swallow it, because a swallowed dose loses much of its strength in the liver
option_4: absorbed into the veins under the tongue and carried to the heart before the liver

question: A patient with a sore throat asks for an antibiotic. The nurse explains that an antibiotic is not given mainly because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. most sore throats are caused by viruses, on which antibiotics do not act

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Antibiotics act on bacteria, and a sore throat is usually caused by a virus, so the drug would do no good and would only help resistant bacteria to grow

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — antibiotics are costly: Cost is not the clinical reason

C — antibiotics are not kept in the hospital: Availability is not the reason

D — antibiotics themselves cause fever: Antibiotics do not by themselves cause fever

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains in one plain sentence why the drug will not help and offers warm saline gargles, because a patient who is only refused feels unheard and buys the antibiotic later over the counter
option_1: most sore throats are caused by viruses, on which antibiotics do not act
option_3: antibiotics are not kept in the hospital

question: The anticoagulant whose effect is monitored by the activated partial thromboplastin time is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. heparin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Heparin acts on the clotting factors already present in the blood, and the activated partial thromboplastin time measures this effect

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — clopidogrel: Clopidogrel acts on the platelets and is not monitored by it

B — warfarin: Warfarin is monitored by the prothrombin time and the INR

C — aspirin: Aspirin is not monitored by this test

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The report is seen before the next dose and the site watched for bleeding, because the effect of heparin shifts with every change of dose and an unmonitored dose can cause bleeding

question: A 60-year-old man on enalapril for high blood pressure develops a troublesome dry cough. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. record the finding and inform the doctor, who may change the drug

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A dry cough is a known effect of this group, and the doctor decides on a change after the nurse has reported it

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell him that the cough has nothing to do with the drug: The cough is a known effect and must not be dismissed

B — stop the drug and give another drug instead: The nurse does not change a prescription

D — give a cough syrup and continue the same drug: A cough syrup does not remove the cause

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also watches for swelling of the face and the tongue, because a rare but severe reaction to this group begins in that way and needs the drug to be stopped at once
option_1: tell him that the cough has nothing to do with the drug
option_2: stop the drug and give another drug instead
option_3: record the finding and inform the doctor, who may change the drug
option_4: give a cough syrup and continue the same drug

question: In diabetic ketoacidosis the insulin chosen for the initial treatment is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a short acting soluble insulin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Soluble insulin acts within half an hour and may be given into the vein, so it is the one used when the patient is gravely ill

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a premixed insulin: A premixed insulin has a fixed combination that cannot be adjusted

C — an intermediate acting insulin: An intermediate acting insulin is too slow

D — a long acting zinc suspension: A long acting suspension acts slowly and is useless in an emergency

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse measures the blood sugar every hour during the infusion, because soluble insulin acts fast and the sugar can fall far below normal if the rate is not watched

question: A concentrated ampoule of potassium chloride is stored apart and labelled clearly because an undiluted dose:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. stops the heart

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A concentrated dose of potassium given quickly stops the heart, and this is why it is always diluted and given slowly

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — raises the blood pressure only: A brief rise in blood pressure is not the chief danger

B — causes vomiting only: Vomiting is not the serious effect

D — causes pain in the arm only: Pain in the arm is a lesser sign of the same danger

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The ampoule is never left at the bedside and the bag is mixed and turned over several times, because a layer of undiluted drug lying at the bottom reaches the heart first

question: A serious adverse drug reaction is reported to the national pharmacovigilance centre mainly so that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. uncommon and serious reactions can be found early and action taken

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A single hospital sees very few reactions, and reports gathered from many hospitals reveal a rare or serious pattern that leads to a warning or a withdrawal

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the drug can be sold at a lower price: Pricing is not its purpose

C — the patient can be charged for the drug: The report is not a billing document

D — the nurse can be given a certificate: The report is not made for an award

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The reaction, the drug, the dose and the time are written plainly on the form, because an incomplete form cannot be used in the analysis and the effort spent on it is wasted
option_1: uncommon and serious reactions can be found early and action taken
option_2: the drug can be sold at a lower price
option_3: the patient can be charged for the drug
option_4: the nurse can be given a certificate

question: The controlled drug register is signed by two nurses at every shift change mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. account for every dose so that any shortage is found at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A running balance signed by two nurses at each change of shift means that any loss is found at once and can be traced to a single shift

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — make the record look complete: The value lies in the check and not in the appearance

B — keep the nurses occupied: It is a safety step and not a way to fill time

D — save time at the end of the day: The check costs time and is done for safety

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The balance is counted in the presence of the nurse going off duty, because a shortage found after that nurse has left cannot be pinned to any shift
option_3: account for every dose so that any shortage is found at once
option_4: save time at the end of the day

question: A 30-year-old man on phenytoin for fits develops tremors, unsteady walking and double vision. The nurse should suspect:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. phenytoin toxicity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Tremors, unsteadiness and double vision appear when the level of phenytoin is above the safe range

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — lack of sleep: Lack of sleep alone does not give this group of signs

B — a low drug level: A low level would allow fits rather than these signs

D — an eye disease: An eye disease would not cause the tremors and the unsteady walk

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dose is held and the level sent as ordered, because a level already above the range keeps rising when the drug is repeated at a fixed dose

question: A patient on antitubercular treatment with rifampicin is warned that his urine and tears may turn:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. orange-red

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rifampicin colours the urine, the sweat and the tears a harmless orange-red

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — deep yellow-green: A yellow-green colour is not caused by this drug

B — blue: Blue urine does not follow this drug

D — black: A black colour is not seen with rifampicin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse warns the patient in advance, because a red colour that appears without warning frightens a patient into stopping a treatment that must be taken for months

question: In poisoning with an organophosphate insecticide, atropine is given along with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. pralidoxime

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pralidoxime reactivates the enzyme that the insecticide has blocked, while atropine blocks the effects of the poison that has already collected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — protamine sulphate: Protamine sulphate reverses heparin

C — vitamin K: Vitamin K reverses warfarin

D — naloxone: Naloxone reverses opioid drugs

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Atropine is repeated until the secretions dry and the pulse picks up, because the amount needed in such poisoning is far larger than in ordinary use and the signs decide the dose

question: A patient asks why a strong antibiotic is not started before the sensitivity report is ready. The nurse explains that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a wrong antibiotic may let the infection worsen and also add to resistance

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Until the organism is known, a wrong choice may let the infection grow and also press the bacteria towards resistance, so the doctor starts the best available drug and changes it when the report comes

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the laboratory is slow: The reason is clinical and not a delay in the laboratory

C — antibiotics act only after a week: The drugs act within hours and not a week

D — antibiotics are costly: Cost is not the main reason

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sends the repeat sample before the next dose while the patient is still on treatment, because the sensitivity of the organism can change and the later report guides a change of drug
option_2: a wrong antibiotic may let the infection worsen and also add to resistance

question: A 26-year-old woman develops a widespread itchy rash with swelling of the lips twenty minutes after a drug is given. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. stop the drug, keep the airway under watch and call the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A rash with swelling of the lips and face warns of a severe allergic reaction, so the drug is stopped, the airway watched and the doctor called at once

🔍 Key Clues: 26-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — apply ice and wait for an hour: Waiting is dangerous while the airway may swell

B — give the next dose along with an antihistamine: Giving the same drug again can be fatal

C — continue the drug and apply a soothing lotion: Continuing the drug deepens the reaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The drug is entered on the allergy record and on the patient's band, because the next exposure can begin within seconds and be far worse than this one
option_1: apply ice and wait for an hour
option_2: give the next dose along with an antihistamine
option_3: continue the drug and apply a soothing lotion
option_4: stop the drug, keep the airway under watch and call the doctor at once

question: The accepted practice before giving a high-alert drug such as insulin is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. have a second nurse check the dose, the drug and the rate independently

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A high-alert drug is checked independently by a second nurse before it is given, and this check catches errors before the patient is harmed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rely on memory of the usual dose: A usual dose is not a substitute for the written order

C — give it quickly to save time: Hurrying removes the very check that keeps the drug safe

D — ask the patient to confirm the dose: The patient does not know the prescribed dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The double check is done at the bedside with the original order in hand, because a check done from memory repeats the same error rather than finding it
option_1: rely on memory of the usual dose
option_2: have a second nurse check the dose, the drug and the rate independently
option_4: ask the patient to confirm the dose

question: A 70-year-old woman on digoxin has a serum potassium of 3.1 mEq/L and a digoxin level at the upper limit of the range. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. hold the dose till the doctor is informed, since a low potassium increases the risk of toxicity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low potassium makes the heart more sensitive to digoxin, so the dose is held until the doctor has been told and the potassium corrected

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old | 3.1 mEq/L

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a potassium supplement without informing anyone: A supplement is not given on the nurse's own decision without reporting this combination

B — give the digoxin as ordered: Giving the dose at the upper limit with a low potassium risks toxicity

D — increase the dose of digoxin: A larger dose would be dangerous

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the two values together, because each is only mildly abnormal on its own and the danger lies in the pair
option_1: give a potassium supplement without informing anyone
option_3: hold the dose till the doctor is informed, since a low potassium increases the risk of toxicity

question: The nurse explains that the amount of a drug reaching the general circulation unchanged is called its:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. bioavailability

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bioavailability is the share of the dose that reaches the general circulation in an active form

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — loading dose: The loading dose is the larger first dose given to fill the body stores quickly

C — half life: The half life is the time taken for the blood level to fall by half

D — therapeutic index: The therapeutic index is the gap between the effective and the toxic dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse understands why the oral and the intravenous dose of the same drug are not equal, because only a part of an oral dose survives the liver and reaches the blood

question: A 55-year-old man on NPH insulin at bedtime has a blood sugar of 48 mg/dL at three in the morning and wakes up sweating. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. treat the low sugar with a fast acting carbohydrate and report the night time low to the doctor

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sweating with a low sugar in the early hours on an intermediate acting insulin means the insulin is peaking at the wrong time, and the low sugar is treated at once and reported

🔍 Key Clues: 55-year-old | 48 mg/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give the usual bedtime dose at once: More insulin would deepen the low sugar

B — give the next dose of insulin early: An early dose is not the answer

C — withhold all food and wait: Withholding food in hypoglycaemia is dangerous

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the sugar at three in the morning for a few nights, because the pattern tells the doctor whether the dose or the timing of the insulin must be changed
option_1: give the usual bedtime dose at once
option_2: give the next dose of insulin early
option_4: treat the low sugar with a fast acting carbohydrate and report the night time low to the doctor

question: A patient on warfarin is advised to keep the intake of green leafy vegetables steady because they:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. contain vitamin K, which opposes the action of warfarin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Green leafy vegetables supply vitamin K, which works against warfarin, so the intake is kept steady rather than stopped

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cause a rash with warfarin: A rash is not the reason

B — increase the bleeding: Bleeding comes from too high a dose and not from the greens

C — lower the blood pressure: Blood pressure is not the concern

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse does not forbid these foods but teaches a steady daily amount, because a sudden change in either direction shifts the INR and defeats the treatment
option_4: contain vitamin K, which opposes the action of warfarin

question: A 40-year-old man on treatment for tuberculosis with ethambutol says he cannot tell red from green. The nurse understands that this is due to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. damage to the optic nerve by the drug

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Ethambutol can damage the optic nerve, and the earliest sign is a loss of the ability to tell red from green

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a vitamin A deficiency: A vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and not this colour defect

C — high blood pressure in the eye: A raised pressure in the eye causes pain and haloes

D — a cataract: A cataract causes a gradual clouding of vision

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks about colour vision at each follow up and reports any change, because this effect is reversible if the drug is stopped early and permanent if it is not
option_2: damage to the optic nerve by the drug

question: After a Gram stain, the Gram positive organisms appear:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. violet or purple

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gram positive organisms keep the violet colour of crystal violet because their thick wall does not let the alcohol wash it out

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — green: A green colour is not seen in a Gram stain

C — colourless: Colourless organisms would mean the stain has failed

D — pink: Pink is the colour of the Gram negative organisms after the counterstain

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes on the request form whether the pus or the fluid looks like the sample wanted, because a poor sample cannot be made good on the slide

question: A 35-year-old woman's urine culture report shows a wide clear zone around the disc of an antibiotic. The nurse understands that this means the organism is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. sensitive to that antibiotic

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The antibiotic spreads out from the disc and stops the growth around it, and the width of the clear zone shows how sensitive the organism is

🔍 Key Clues: 35-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — resistant to that antibiotic: A resistant organism would grow right up to the disc

C — not growing at all in the sample: No growth at all would give a sterile report

D — contaminated with a second organism: A second organism shows as a separate type of colony

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the sensitivity line together with the name of the organism, because the drug that is sensitive in the laboratory may still be unsuitable for this particular patient
option_3: not growing at all in the sample

question: A stool sample for culture must be sent to the laboratory:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. in a clean container, without delay, and free from urine and water

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The stool is collected in a clean container and sent quickly, and urine or water must not be mixed with it, because these change the growth of the organisms

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — after keeping it warm for a day: A sample kept warm for a day grows over with other organisms and is useless

C — mixed with tap water to prevent drying: Tap water dilutes the sample and may carry organisms of its own

D — only after the patient has been given an antibiotic: An antibiotic would suppress the very organism that is being looked for

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: A small quantity of the stool taken from the portion that contains mucus or blood is more useful than a large plain sample, because the organisms collect in the abnormal part
option_1: in a clean container, without delay, and free from urine and water
option_2: after keeping it warm for a day
option_3: mixed with tap water to prevent drying
option_4: only after the patient has been given an antibiotic

question: The indicator tape on the outside of an autoclave pack turns dark after the cycle. This shows that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the pack has been through the sterilising cycle

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The tape reacts to the heat and moisture of the cycle and shows only that the load was processed, not that every article inside is sterile

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the pack is now sterile for use for a month: The tape does not give a date of sterility

C — the pack is still wet: A wet pack is judged by touch and is a separate defect

D — the autoclave has cooled: The colour change is not a measure of cooling

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the date on the pack and uses the older packs first, because the tape tells of the past cycle and not of the day the pack is opened
option_1: the pack has been through the sterilising cycle
option_2: the pack is now sterile for use for a month

question: A sample for anaerobic culture must be transported:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. in a special container with the air excluded, without delay

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Anaerobic organisms are killed by oxygen, so the sample is kept out of contact with air and sent without delay

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — in an open jar exposed to air: Exposure to air kills the very organisms that are being looked for

C — in a dry cotton swab with no medium: A dry swab carries too little material and dies quickly

D — in water at room temperature: Plain water is not a suitable medium

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sends the pus from a deep abscess in the special container as soon as it is collected, because even a few minutes in the air can turn a positive culture into a wasted report
option_1: in a special container with the air excluded, without delay
option_2: in an open jar exposed to air
option_3: in a dry cotton swab with no medium

question: A 45-year-old man suspected of pulmonary tuberculosis is to send sputum for the acid fast stain. The nurse instructs him to collect:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. three early morning samples on three consecutive days from deep within the chest

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Three early morning samples taken from deep in the chest raise the chance of finding the bacilli, and the morning sputum is the richest

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a single sample mixed with tap water: Water dilutes the sample and lowers the yield

B — a sample taken two hours after starting the antibiotics: Antibiotics already started reduce the number of bacilli in the sample

C — one sample of saliva in the evening: Saliva and an evening sample give a poor yield

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse supervises the collection and shows the patient how to cough from the chest, because a sample that is really saliva gives a negative report and delays the start of treatment
option_1: a single sample mixed with tap water
option_2: a sample taken two hours after starting the antibiotics
option_3: one sample of saliva in the evening
option_4: three early morning samples on three consecutive days from deep within the chest

question: Before taking a temperature on the next patient, a 30-year-old nurse cleans the clinical thermometer with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a swab of seventy per cent alcohol and lets it dry

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Seventy per cent alcohol kills the organisms on the surface and the thermometer is allowed to dry before use on the next patient

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — soap and a dry cloth: Soap and a dry cloth do not disinfect

B — plain water: Plain water only removes the visible dirt

C — a paper tissue: A paper tissue can carry organisms from one patient to the next

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse rubs from the clean bulb end towards the part held in the hand and lets the alcohol dry, because a wet thermometer carries alcohol into the mouth and gives a false low reading
option_4: a swab of seventy per cent alcohol and lets it dry

question: A urine sample for culture from a patient with an indwelling catheter is best taken:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. with a sterile syringe from a freshly clamped sampling port after cleaning it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The sample is taken from the port made for the purpose, after cleaning it, with a sterile syringe, so that the organisms already growing in the bag are not counted

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — from the drainage tube near the floor: The tube near the floor is heavily contaminated

C — from the urine bag after an hour: Urine in the bag has stood and grown organisms

D — from the dependent loop of the tubing: The dependent loop holds stagnant urine that has collected organisms

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse clamps the tube for a short while and takes the sample from the port, because a sample from the bag so often reports a false infection and leads to needless antibiotics
option_1: from the drainage tube near the floor
option_2: with a sterile syringe from a freshly clamped sampling port after cleaning it
option_3: from the urine bag after an hour
option_4: from the dependent loop of the tubing

question: A 50-year-old man's urine is cloudy, has a strong ammoniacal smell and shows a pH of 8.5. The nurse understands that this suggests:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. an infection with organisms that split urea

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Some bacteria split the urea in the urine into ammonia, which makes the urine alkaline and gives it a strong smell

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a normal urine sample: A normal fresh urine is clear and slightly acid

C — diabetes mellitus: Diabetes gives sugar and ketones

D — a high protein diet: A high protein diet does not make the urine alkaline in this way

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sends the sample for culture and encourages fluids, because a urine left standing and alkaline lets the organisms grow and the infection climb to the kidney
option_2: an infection with organisms that split urea

question: The urine of a patient with obstructive jaundice is most likely to appear:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. dark yellow-brown, with froth that is also yellow

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the flow of bile is blocked the bile salts and pigments pass into the blood and then into the urine, which becomes dark and gives yellow froth on shaking

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — bright red: Bright red points to fresh blood

B — smoky brown: A smoky brown colour points to blood or to myoglobin

D — clear and colourless: A clear urine does not fit an obstruction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes the colour of the stool as well, because a pale clay coloured stool with dark urine is the pair that points most clearly to an obstruction of the bile duct
option_3: dark yellow-brown, with froth that is also yellow

question: The normal packed cell volume in an adult man is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 40 to 50 per cent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The packed cell volume, or haematocrit, is the share of the blood taken up by the cells and lies between about 40 and 50 per cent in an adult man

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 55 to 65 per cent: 55 to 65 per cent is too high and points to a thickened blood

B — 70 to 80 per cent: 70 to 80 per cent is not compatible with normal blood

C — 20 to 30 per cent: 20 to 30 per cent is far too low and means severe anaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse compares this value with the haemoglobin on the same report, because the two should rise and fall together and a gap between them points to a change in the plasma volume

question: A 25-year-old man rescued from under a fallen wall has cola coloured urine and a urine dipstick positive for blood but no red cells on microscopy. The nurse understands that this is due to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. myoglobin from damaged muscle reaching the urine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Crushed muscle releases myoglobin, which colours the urine and gives a positive test for blood although no red cells are seen under the microscope

🔍 Key Clues: 25-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a drug reaction: A drug reaction would not follow a crush injury

C — a urinary infection: An infection gives pus cells

D — a kidney stone: A stone gives red cells as well as blood

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The urine output is measured and the doctor told at once, because myoglobin blocks the kidney tubules and a good flow of urine is the main protection against kidney failure
option_1: myoglobin from damaged muscle reaching the urine

question: The normal total white blood cell count in an adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 4,000 to 11,000 per cubic mm

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The normal white cell count is four thousand to eleven thousand per cubic mm, and the cells defend the body against infection

A — 150,000 to 400,000 per cubic mm: One hundred and fifty to four hundred thousand is the platelet count

C — 500 to 1,500 per cubic mm: Five hundred to one thousand five hundred is far too low and would leave the patient defenceless

D — 50,000 to 70,000 per cubic mm: Fifty to seventy thousand is a leukaemic range

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

question: A set of blood cultures grows the same organism in both bottles within a day of collection. The nurse understands that this most likely means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. there is a true infection in the blood stream

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the same organism grows in both bottles of a set and grows quickly, a real infection in the blood stream is the likely cause

A — the sample was collected from the infusion line: A sample from a line may be contaminated but does not explain growth in both bottles

C — the skin was not cleaned properly: A skin contaminant usually grows in one bottle only and grows slowly

D — the bottles were old: Age of the bottle is not judged from the growth

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes the time of collection on the form, because the speed of growth from the time of collection helps the doctor to judge whether the organism is truly in the blood

option_2: there is a true infection in the blood stream

question: A patient with blood group O who needs red cells must be given blood of group:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. O

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A person of group O has antibodies against both A and B, so only group O red cells can be given safely

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — AB: Group AB cells carry both antigens and are the most dangerous for this patient

B — B: Group B cells carry the B antigen and would be destroyed

question: The usual INR in a person who is not taking any anticoagulant is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 0.8 to 1.2

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a person not on an anticoagulant the INR is about 1, that is between 0.8 and 1.2

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 3.5 to 4.5: Three and a half to four and a half is above the usual target and carries a bleeding risk

C — 5.0 to 6.0: Five to six is a dangerously high value

D — 2.0 to 3.0: Two to three is the target range for most patients on warfarin

question: The normal blood urea level in an adult is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 15 to 45 mg/dL

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The normal blood urea lies between about 15 and 45 mg/dL and rises when the kidney is not clearing the waste well

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 150 to 200 mg/dL: 150 to 200 mg/dL points to marked kidney failure

C — 5 to 15 mg/dL: 5 to 15 mg/dL is lower than the usual range

D — 80 to 120 mg/dL: 80 to 120 mg/dL is raised

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

question: A patient's arterial blood shows a pH of 7.25 with a bicarbonate of 16 mEq/L. The nurse understands that this is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. metabolic acidosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low pH with a low bicarbonate is metabolic acidosis, seen in uncontrolled diabetes and in severe diarrhoea

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — metabolic alkalosis: Metabolic alkalosis gives a high pH with a high bicarbonate

B — respiratory alkalosis: Respiratory alkalosis gives a high pH

C — normal blood gas values: The pH here is outside the normal range

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes the rate and depth of breathing with the report, because the deep rapid breathing of acidosis is the body's attempt to blow off acid and it is the earliest sign the nurse can see

question: A patient with long standing liver disease has a serum albumin of 2.2 g/dL. The nurse understands that this is because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the liver is making too little protein

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Albumin is made in the liver, so a failing liver makes too little of it and the level falls

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the kidney is losing water: Loss of water would make the blood more concentrated

C — the patient has a urinary infection: A urinary infection does not lower the albumin in this way

D — the diet is too rich in protein: A protein rich diet raises rather than lowers the albumin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse watches for swelling of the legs and the abdomen, because a low albumin lets fluid leak into the tissues and the patient gains weight without taking more food
option_1: the liver is making too little protein
option_4: the diet is too rich in protein

question: The blood glucose level of a healthy adult two hours after a meal is usually:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. below 140 mg/dL

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Two hours after a meal the blood sugar of a healthy adult settles to below about 140 mg/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 220 to 250 mg/dL: 220 to 250 mg/dL is clearly raised

C — above 300 mg/dL: A value above 300 mg/dL in this setting is very high

D — 180 to 200 mg/dL: 180 to 200 mg/dL after a meal points to diabetes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses this two hour value along with the fasting value, because a normal fasting sugar with a high two hour value still points to diabetes

question: A 70-year-old man is admitted with a fractured hip. Before the first dose of an analgesic is given, the nurse must first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. check the identity from the name band against the written order

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

A — look at the bed number on the chart: The bed number is not an identifier and beds are changed often

D — take the word of the attendant: An attendant is not a reliable source

option_3: ask the patient his name from the door

question: The single most effective way of preventing the spread of infection in the ward is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. washing the hands at the right moments

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Clean hands at the right moments, before touching a patient and after a dirty task, break the chain of infection more than any other single step

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keeping the windows closed: Closing the windows keeps stale air in and helps no one

B — wearing gloves all the time: Gloves are worn for a task and do not replace hand washing

D — changing the bed linen daily: Fresh linen helps but is not the main step

option_3: washing the hands at the right moments

question: A 40-year-old woman's blood is taken for a cross match. The nurse must label the sample tube:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. at the bedside, filling the label and the form with her own signature and the time

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

option_2: at the bedside, filling the label and the form with her own signature and the time
option_3: at the station after all the rounds are over

question: A patient is taught about his medicines before discharge mainly because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. he must continue the treatment correctly at home

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Teaching before discharge prepares the patient to take the right drug in the right dose at the right time when the ward staff are no longer there

A — it saves the nurse's time on the next visit: The aim is the patient's safety and not the nurse's time

C — the doctor has asked for it: The reason is clinical and not merely an order

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks the patient to say back what he will do, because a patient who can repeat the instructions in his own words is far more likely to follow them
option_1: it saves the nurse's time on the next visit
option_2: he must continue the treatment correctly at home

question: A 50-year-old man is to receive 1,000 mL of normal saline over eight hours with a set that gives 20 drops per mL. The rate is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 42 drops per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One thousand millilitres multiplied by twenty gives 20,000 drops, and divided by 480 minutes this is about 42 drops a minute

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old | 000 mL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 50 drops per minute: Fifty drops a minute would finish the bottle in under seven hours

B — 30 drops per minute: Thirty drops a minute would take more than eleven hours

D — 60 drops per minute: Sixty drops a minute is far more than the order

question: A 30-year-old woman is to be given a unit of packed red cells. During the first fifteen minutes the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. stay with her and run the blood slowly while watching for any reaction

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Most severe reactions begin in the first fifteen minutes, so the nurse stays and keeps the rate slow during that time

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

B — warm the blood in hot water: Blood is never warmed in hot water, which damages the cells

C — run the blood fast and leave the bedside: A fast rate in a patient left alone hides the earliest signs

question: Ten minutes into a blood transfusion a patient develops chills, a rising temperature and pain in the lower back. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. stop the transfusion, keep the line open with normal saline and inform the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Fever with chills and back pain points to a haemolytic reaction, and the transfusion is stopped at once while the line is kept open with saline and the doctor is called

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — slow the transfusion and wait: Slowing the flow still gives the patient more of the wrong blood

C — roll the patient to one side: Turning the patient does not help

D — give a dose of paracetamol and continue: A drug does not stop the reaction and delays the action

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

option_2: stop the transfusion, keep the line open with normal saline and inform the doctor at once
option_4: give a dose of paracetamol and continue

question: Oxygen is passed through water before it is given to a patient mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. moisten it so that the airway does not dry

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The humidifier adds water vapour so that the dry gas does not dry the lining of the nose and the throat

A — remove the carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide is not removed by this bottle

B — measure the flow: The flow is set on the flow meter

option_3: moisten it so that the airway does not dry

question: Before a feed is given through a nasogastric tube the nurse confirms the position of the tube by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. aspirating the stomach contents and checking their pH

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Aspirating the contents and testing the pH is the reliable bedside method, since a stomach aspirate is acid

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — listening for a bubbling sound after pushing air: The auscultation of air is no longer relied on because the sound can be heard with the tube in the lung

B — asking the patient to speak: Some patients can speak with an incorrectly placed tube

option_4: aspirating the stomach contents and checking their pH

question: The normal resting pulse rate in an adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 60 to 100 per minute

A — 140 to 160 per minute: 140 to 160 is the normal range for a newborn

question: A patient is ordered 250 mg of a drug, and the vial contains 500 mg in 2 mL. The nurse draws up:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1 mL

A — 2 mL: 2 mL is the whole vial, which is 500 mg

question: The first stage of labour ends when:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the cervix is fully dilated

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The first stage lasts from the onset of regular pains to full dilatation of the cervix, which begins the second stage

A — the membranes rupture: The membranes may rupture at any time and do not mark the end of the stage

B — the baby is born: The birth of the baby ends the second stage

C — the placenta is delivered: The delivery of the placenta is the third stage

question: A woman in labour has a sudden gush of fluid and the nurse feels a pulsating cord in the vagina. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. relieve the pressure on the cord by lifting the presenting part and place her knee chest, calling for help

question: The normal fetal heart rate lies between:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 120 and 160 per minute

question: In the active management of the third stage of labour, the uterotonic drug is given:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. within a minute of the birth of the baby, after ruling out a second baby

question: The cold chain for vaccines means:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. keeping each vaccine within its own required temperature from the factory to the child

question: On a home visit a nurse finds a 3-year-old child with fever, a rash that began behind the ears and a running nose, and the child has never been immunised. The nurse should first:

question: The single best measure of the general health of a community is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. infant mortality rate

question: The safe disposal of human waste in a village prevents mainly:
solution:

question: By the age of six months an infant should have completed:

question: A 3-year-old child with severe wasting and no swelling is admitted to the nutrition unit. The nurse should first:

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The normal resting rate in an adult lies between 12 and 20 breaths a minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 24 to 30 per minute: Twenty-four to thirty is tachypnoea

C — 6 to 10 per minute: Six to ten is too slow

D — 30 to 40 per minute: Thirty to forty is the rate of a young child

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse counts the breaths without telling the patient, because breathing changes as soon as a person knows it is being watched

question: The pressure inside the pleural cavity is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. slightly negative to the outside air

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The pressure in the pleural cavity is slightly lower than the air outside, and this negative pressure keeps the lungs expanded against the chest wall

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the same as the outside air: It is not equal to the outside air

B — always above the outside air: A positive pressure is abnormal and means a leak

D — always equal to the blood pressure: It is not equal to the blood pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse understands why air entering the chest through a wound causes the lung to fall in, and covers such a wound at once with an airtight dressing

question: The average life span of a red blood cell in the circulation is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 120 days

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A red cell survives about 120 days and is then broken up, and new cells replace it from the marrow

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7 days: Seven days is much too short

B — 30 days: Thirty days is only a quarter of the life span

D — 365 days: A whole year is far too long

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse links this to the result of a transfusion, because the benefit lasts only as long as the cells survive and the haemoglobin therefore falls again after some weeks

question: A patient who has just started an antidepressant is told that the full benefit will appear only after:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. two to four weeks

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The drugs take about two to four weeks to act fully, and the patient is told this so that he does not stop the medicine early

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a few hours: A response in a few hours does not occur

B — six to eight months: Six to eight months is far longer than the time to act

D — the first dose: A single dose does not work

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the patient under close watch in the first weeks, because the energy to act often returns before the mood lifts and this is the period of greatest risk

question: A patient on an antipsychotic drug develops a high fever, stiff muscles and a rapid pulse. The nurse should suspect:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. neuroleptic malignant syndrome

🧠 Clinical Rationale: High fever, stiff muscles and a rapid pulse together are the features of neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a rare and dangerous reaction

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a common cold: A cold does not cause the muscle stiffness

B — a drug allergy: An allergy shows as a rash

D — a urinary infection: A urinary infection does not stiffen the muscles

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The drug is stopped and the doctor called at once, and the nurse records the temperature and the pulse frequently, because this reaction can end in kidney failure if it is not treated early

question: A patient whose gums bleed on brushing and whose wounds heal slowly is most likely short of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. vitamin C

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin C is needed for the making of the ground substance of the tissues, so its lack gives bleeding gums and slow healing

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — vitamin D: A lack of vitamin D causes rickets and soft bones

C — vitamin K: A lack of vitamin K causes bleeding from a delay in clotting and not from the gums in this way

D — vitamin A: A lack of vitamin A causes night blindness

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse adds guava, amla and other fresh fruit to the diet, because the vitamin is destroyed by long cooking and a boiled diet gives too little of it

question: In delegation the nurse manager understands that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the task is given to another person while the accountability stays with her

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A task can be handed over, but the nurse remains answerable for it, so she must choose a person able to do it and then follow it up

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the responsibility and the accountability both pass to the other person: Accountability cannot be handed over

B — she need not know the ability of the other person: The ability of the person is checked before the task is given

D — any task may be delegated to anyone: Only the tasks within the person's training and the rules may be delegated

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains the task, the limits and the time to report back, because a task given without limits leaves a junior unsure how far to go and when to call for help

question: In an experiment the group that does not receive the treatment being tested is called the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. control group

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The control group is managed in the same way but without the treatment under study, so that the two groups can be compared fairly

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — study group: A study group is a general term and not the group kept without the treatment

B — sample group: The sample is the whole set of persons drawn from the population

D — experimental group: The experimental group is the one that receives the treatment

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains that both groups are otherwise cared for alike, because if the control group gets better care in other ways the comparison says nothing about the treatment

question: Who was the first woman to become the Chief Minister of an Indian state?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Sucheta Kripalani

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sucheta Kripalani became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1963, the first woman to hold that office in any Indian state

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit held other high offices and not this one

B — Sarojini Naidu: Sarojini Naidu was the Governor of Uttar Pradesh and not its Chief Minister

C — Indira Gandhi: Indira Gandhi became Prime Minister and not the Chief Minister of a state

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: A nurse who knows how women entered public life finds it easier to explain to a village why a woman health worker is the right person to speak about the health of the mothers in that village

question: The Indian state that has the largest area is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Rajasthan

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rajasthan covers the greatest area of any Indian state, being largely desert with a thinly spread population

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Madhya Pradesh: Madhya Pradesh is large but smaller than Rajasthan

C — Uttar Pradesh: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state but not the largest in area

D — Maharashtra: Maharashtra is smaller than both

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse working in a thinly populated district plans the immunisation rounds by distance rather than by numbers, because a few children may be spread over many kilometres

question: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 2013

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in 2013 to set up an ombudsman for complaints against public servants

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 2005: 2005 is the year of the Right to Information Act

B — 2016: 2016 is later than its passing

C — 2011: 2011 is earlier than the passing of this Act

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows that a complaint about any public office has a set channel, and this is the same spirit that makes an incident reporting form in the hospital useful rather than merely a record

question: The maximum number of members of the Rajya Sabha provided by the Constitution is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 250

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Constitution provides a maximum of 250 members for the Rajya Sabha, of whom twelve are nominated by the President

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 200: Two hundred is below the stated maximum

B — 552: Five hundred and fifty two is the maximum fixed for the Lok Sabha

C — 238: Two hundred and thirty eight is the number of members elected from the states and the two union territories

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows how a health bill becomes law understands why the profession must speak to members of both houses when a law on nursing practice is being framed

question: The Fundamental Duties of the citizens were added to the Constitution by which amendment?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the 42nd Amendment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 on the advice of the Swaran Singh Committee

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the 44th Amendment: The 44th Amendment removed the right to property from the fundamental rights

C — the 52nd Amendment: The 52nd Amendment dealt with the anti defection law

D — the 24th Amendment: The 24th Amendment dealt with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the duty to protect the public property and the natural environment as applying directly to the way the ward equipment and the hospital waste are handled

question: The Green Revolution in India is chiefly associated with a rise in the production of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. foodgrains

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Green Revolution raised the output of wheat and rice through better seeds, water and fertiliser

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cotton: Cotton is a cash crop and not the concern of the Green Revolution

B — fish: A rise in fish production is the Blue Revolution

D — milk: A rise in milk production is called the White Revolution

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse links a better food supply with the fall in severe malnutrition in a district, because a health centre alone can do little when the fields around it give too little food

question: The Nobel Prize awarded to C V Raman was for his work on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the scattering of light

🧠 Clinical Rationale: C V Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his work on the scattering of light, now called the Raman effect

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the speed of light: The speed of light was measured by others and long before

B — the splitting of the atom: The splitting of the atom is the work of a different group of physicists

D — the structure of the atom: The structure of the atom was explained by others

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse can turn such a fact into a small talk with a patient, because a patient who is drawn into a conversation becomes less anxious and easier to examine

question: The Indian National Congress was founded in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1885

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 and became the main platform of the national movement

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1905: 1905 is the year of the partition of Bengal

C — 1857: 1857 is the year of the first war of independence

D — 1920: 1920 is the year of the non cooperation movement

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows how a large body of people was organised for a single cause understands why a community health programme must be taken to the people and not merely announced in an office

question: The unit of force in the SI system is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. newton

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Force is measured in newtons, one newton being the force that gives a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second each second

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — watt: The watt is the unit of power

C — pascal: The pascal is the unit of pressure

D — joule: The joule is the unit of energy and work

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse understands that pressure is force on an area, and this is why the same weight spread over a wide surface does far less harm to the skin than a narrow one

question: The plant tissue that carries water from the root to the leaves is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. xylem

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The xylem is the tissue that carries water and the dissolved salts upwards from the root to the leaves

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cambium: The cambium is the growing layer between the xylem and the phloem

B — phloem: The phloem carries the food made in the leaves to the other parts

C — cork: The cork forms the outer protective layer of the stem

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse draws the parallel with the body when teaching about the circulation, because children remember the two way traffic of the plant far more easily than a diagram of the blood vessels

question: During photosynthesis green plants take in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. carbon dioxide

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Green plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen while making their food in the light

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — hydrogen: Free hydrogen is not taken in by plants

C — nitrogen: Nitrogen is taken from the soil through the roots as salts

D — oxygen: Oxygen is given out and not taken in

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains why a crowded ward with the windows shut becomes stuffy, and why fresh air is part of the care of a breathless patient

question: The hardest substance in the human body is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. enamel of the teeth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The enamel covering the teeth is the hardest substance in the body and resists the wear of chewing

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — cartilage: Cartilage is soft and flexible

C — bone: Bone is hard but not as hard as enamel

D — tendon: A tendon is tough but not hard

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse teaches a pregnant woman to rinse the mouth after every vomiting, because the stomach acid softens the enamel and brushing at once wears it away

question: The normal body temperature of a healthy adult, measured in the mouth, is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 37 degrees Celsius

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The normal temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius when measured in the mouth, with a small daily variation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 41 degrees Celsius: 41 degrees Celsius is a very high fever and is dangerous

B — 39 degrees Celsius: 39 degrees Celsius is a fever

C — 35 degrees Celsius: 35 degrees Celsius is below normal and points to a low body temperature

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the site along with the reading, because the temperature in the armpit is about half a degree lower than in the mouth and the same patient can appear to improve if the site is changed

question: The pH of the contents of the normal stomach is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 1 to 3

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The stomach secretes acid and its contents are strongly acid, with a pH of about 1 to 3

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7 to 8: Seven is neutral

B — 9 to 10: A pH of 9 to 10 is alkaline and belongs to the small intestine in part

C — 5 to 6: A pH of 5 to 6 is far less acid than the stomach

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes when a patient is on a drug that lowers the acid, because the aspirate from a feeding tube then gives a raised pH and the tube position must be judged with extra care

question: The largest part of the human brain is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. cerebrum

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is the seat of thought, memory, speech and voluntary movement

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — medulla oblongata: The medulla oblongata is a small part at the base of the brain

C — cerebellum: The cerebellum is smaller and lies below and behind the cerebrum

D — hypothalamus: The hypothalamus is a small region below the thalamus

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes which side of the body is weak and whether speech is lost, because the cerebrum is divided into two halves and each half controls the opposite side of the body

question: The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. pulmonary vein

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The pulmonary vein brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left side of the heart, and it is the vein that carries oxygenated blood

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pulmonary artery: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs

B — aorta: The aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the whole body

D — vena cava: The vena cava brings deoxygenated blood back from the body

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse remembers this exception when reading a report of a chest injury, because bleeding into the chest may come from a vessel carrying oxygen rich blood

question: A 60 kg patient is prescribed 8 mg per kg per day of a drug in two divided doses. The dose at each time is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 240 mg

🧠 Method: Eight multiplied by sixty gives 480 mg for the day, and divided by two this is 240 mg at each dose

🔍 Key Clues: 60 kg

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 480 mg: 480 mg is the whole day's dose in one take

B — 960 mg: 960 mg is twice the day's dose

C — 120 mg: 120 mg would be only a quarter of the day's dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Multiply the dose per kilogram by the weight first and divide by the number of doses afterwards, because dividing the dose per kilogram before multiplying invites a decimal slip

question: If three nurses can prepare fifteen trays in an hour, how many trays can five nurses prepare in the same time?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 25

🧠 Method: Three nurses prepare fifteen trays, so one nurse prepares five, and five nurses prepare twenty five trays

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 35: 35 would need seven nurses

C — 30: 30 would need six nurses

D — 20: 20 would need only four nurses

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Find the value for one first and then multiply, because this single step turns most proportion questions into simple multiplication

question: The weights of five newborn babies are 2.4, 2.6, 2.8, 3.0 and 3.2 kilograms. The average weight is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 2.8 kg

🧠 Method: The total is fourteen kilograms and there are five babies, so fourteen divided by five gives 2.8 kg

🔍 Key Clues: newborn

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 2.6 kg: 2.6 kg is the second weight and not the average

C — 3.2 kg: 3.2 kg is the highest weight

D — 3.0 kg: 3.0 kg is the fourth weight

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Add all the weights and count the babies before dividing, because the middle value of a set and the average are not the same thing

question: A strip of tablets costs 24 rupees and is sold for 30 rupees. The profit per cent is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 25 per cent

🧠 Method: The profit is six rupees on a cost of twenty four, and six divided by twenty four multiplied by hundred gives twenty five per cent

⚡ Fast Approach: Profit percent is always on the cost price, loss percent also on the cost price.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 20 per cent: Twenty per cent would be a profit of only 4.80 rupees

C — 6 per cent: Six per cent is the profit in rupees misread as a percentage

D — 30 per cent: Thirty per cent would take the cost as the selling price

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Profit per cent is always taken on the cost price and not on the selling price, because this one difference changes the answer in every profit and loss question

question: A nurse walks three kilometres in forty five minutes. The speed in kilometres per hour is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 4

🧠 Method: Forty five minutes is three quarters of an hour, and three divided by three quarters gives four kilometres an hour

⚡ Fast Approach: Average speed = total distance / total time - never the mean of the two speeds.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 5: Five kilometres an hour is faster than the walk described

B — 6: Six kilometres an hour is much faster

C — 3: Three kilometres an hour would take an hour for three kilometres

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Change the minutes into a fraction of an hour before dividing, because a speed worked out with the time left in minutes is wrong by a factor of sixty

question: The least number that must be added to 1537 to make it exactly divisible by 9 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 2

🧠 Method: The sum of the digits is sixteen, and the next multiple of nine is eighteen, so two must be added

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 3: Adding three gives nineteen

B — 5: Adding five gives twenty one

C — 1: Adding one gives a digit sum of seventeen, which is not a multiple of nine

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Use the digit sum test for divisibility by nine instead of long division, because the digit sum can be taken at a glance and saves a whole step

question: A ten per cent solution is diluted to make a two per cent solution. The final volume will be how many times the original volume?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 5

🧠 Method: The amount of the solute does not change, so ten divided by two gives five times the original volume

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 3: Three times would give about a three per cent solution

C — 8: Eight times would give far less than two per cent

D — 2: Twice would give a five per cent solution

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Remember that the solute stays the same and only the volume changes, because this is the whole of every dilution sum

question: Find the odd one out: doctor, nurse, teacher, stethoscope.
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. stethoscope

🧠 Method: The doctor, the nurse and the teacher are persons, while the stethoscope is an instrument

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — doctor: A doctor is a person who works in health care

C — nurse: A nurse is also a person

D — teacher: A teacher is a person who works in education

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Name the property that the first three share in one word before choosing, because the odd one out is the item that does not fit that single property

question: Thermometer is to temperature as sphygmomanometer is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. blood pressure

🧠 Method: A thermometer measures temperature and a sphygmomanometer measures blood pressure, so the instrument and the quantity it measures form the pair

⚡ Fast Approach: State the relationship in words first, then look for the same relationship.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pulse: The pulse is counted by the fingers and not by this instrument

B — temperature: Temperature is measured by the thermometer already named

C — respiratory rate: The respiratory rate is counted by watching the chest

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: State the relation in a few words first and then look for the same relation in the options, because a familiar sounding pair is often the wrong one

question: If HEALTH is written as IFBMUI, then NURSE is written as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. OVSTF

🧠 Method: Each letter is moved one step forward in the alphabet, so N U R S E becomes O V S T F

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — OUSTF: The second letter U in place of V breaks the pattern

C — OVSFT: The last two letters are interchanged

D — PVSTF: The first letter P is two steps ahead of N

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Apply the rule to the first two letters and then write the whole word, because a single letter out of place makes the whole option wrong

question: If A is numbered 1, B is numbered 2 and so on, the sum of the letters of the word BAT is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 23

🧠 Method: B is 2, A is 1 and T is 20, so the sum is 23

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 26: 26 is the value of the last letter of the alphabet

C — 22: 22 would need the last letter to be worth one less

D — 24: 24 would need one letter to be worth one more

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Write the value under each letter before adding, because adding the letters as they are read is where a slip most often occurs

question: A is the brother of B. B is the sister of C. C is the father of D. How is A related to D?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. uncle

🧠 Method: A, B and C are brothers and sisters, and C is the father of D, so A is the uncle of D

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — brother: A is the brother of C and not of D

B — grandfather: A is of the same generation as the father of D and not of the generation above

D — father: The father of D is C and not A

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Draw the tree with each generation on one level before answering, because relations that skip a generation are where most mistakes are made

question: A man facing north turns 90 degrees to his right, then 180 degrees, then 90 degrees to his left. Which direction is he facing now?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. south

🧠 Method: Facing north he turns right to face east, then half a turn to face west, and then left to face south

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — west: West is the direction after the second turn

B — north: North is the direction he began with

D — east: East is the direction after the first turn only

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Draw the four directions and move the pen step by step, because holding all three turns in the head is where the answer usually slips in these questions

question: In a class of 50 students, Meera ranks eighteenth from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 33rd

🧠 Method: The rank from the bottom is the total plus one minus the rank from the top, so 50 plus 1 minus 18 gives 33

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 31st: 31 would need a rank of 20 from the top
